title: Windows and effects
description: Gaps, borders, blur, shadows and how windows behave; changes apply instantly.

sections.title: Game Mode
sections.description: Game Mode temporarily replaces some of these effects for performance.

sections.title: Spacing and borders
sections.description: Space around windows and the shape of their borders.

sections.title: Blur
sections.description: Frosted-glass effect behind the bar, panels, dock, notifications and launcher; windows themselves are never blurred.

sections.title: Shadows
sections.description: Soft shadow around floating windows; tiled windows have none.

sections.title: Dimming
sections.description: Darken windows you are not using to keep attention on the active one.

sections.title: Opacity
sections.description: Make windows see-through; 100 % is fully solid.

sections.title: Behavior
sections.description: How new windows are placed and focused, plus display options for games.

sections.title: Workspaces
sections.description: How you move between workspaces and where new apps open.

sections.title: Gestures
sections.description: Four-finger horizontal swipes on the touchpad switch workspaces.

sections.title: Window rules
sections.description: Per-app rules such as always floating or a fixed workspace.

entries.label: Game Mode is on
entries.description: While it is on, Game Mode turns off blur, shadows and animations, removes gaps and rounding, makes borders 1 px thin and allows tearing; your values are kept and come back when you turn it off.

entries.label: Preview
entries.description: A sketch of your desktop with these values; the magnifier shows one window corner at its real size.

entries.label: Gaps between windows
entries.description: Space on each side of a tiled window that faces another window, in pixels.
entries.help: Two neighbors each keep this gap, so the space between them is twice the value. The same value is used on all four sides.

entries.label: Gaps at the screen edges
entries.description: Space between windows and the edges of the monitor, in pixels.
entries.help: The same value is used on all four edges. The bar keeps its own space on top of it.
keywords: Espacio en los bordes de la pantalla

entries.label: Border width
entries.description: Colored line drawn outside each window, in pixels; 0 hides it.

entries.label: Corner radius
entries.description: How far the rounding of each window corner reaches, in pixels; 0 gives square corners.

entries.label: Corner curve
entries.description: Shape of the rounding: 1 cuts the corner diagonally, 2 is a quarter circle, 4 or more gives smooth squircle corners.

entries.label: Resize from borders
entries.description: Drag a window's border or the gap next to it to change its size.

entries.label: Effects preview
entries.description: The same sketch with blur behind the bar and panels, the floating window's shadow, opacity and dimming.

entries.label: Blur the bar and panels
entries.description: What is behind the bar, panels, dock, notifications and launcher looks frosted.

entries.label: Size
entries.description: How far each pass spreads; bigger looks softer.

entries.label: Passes
entries.description: Each pass blurs the result again: stronger blur, more GPU work.

entries.label: Blur only the wallpaper
entries.description: Blurred surfaces show the wallpaper behind them and ignore the windows in between.
entries.help: The dotfiles turn this on for every shell panel in rules.lua, so panels already show only the wallpaper.

entries.label: Blur menus and popups
entries.description: Also blur behind right-click menus and other popups of apps.

entries.label: Shadow behind floating windows
entries.description: Draw a soft shadow around floating windows and dialogs.

entries.label: Size
entries.description: How far the shadow reaches from the window edge, in pixels.

entries.label: Sharpness
entries.description: Higher values make the shadow edge sharper and shorter.

entries.label: Dim inactive windows
entries.description: Darken every window except the one you are typing in.

entries.label: Strength
entries.description: How dark inactive windows become; 100 % would make them black.

entries.label: Dim behind the scratchpad
entries.description: How much the screen darkens behind the scratchpad workspace (Super+S).
entries.help: The scratchpad is a hidden workspace that appears over the current one; Super+S shows or hides it.

entries.label: Active window
entries.description: How solid the window you are using looks.

entries.label: Inactive windows
entries.description: How solid the other windows look; lower lets the wallpaper show through.

entries.label: Fullscreen windows
entries.description: How solid a window looks while it fills the screen.

entries.label: Keep split direction
entries.description: A window keeps its side-by-side or stacked split when its neighbors open, close or resize.

entries.label: Split by pointer position
entries.description: A new window opens on the side of the current one where the pointer is.

entries.label: Focus windows that ask for it
entries.description: Jump to a window when an app asks for attention, e.g. opening a link brings the browser forward.

entries.label: Hide the terminal behind apps it opens
entries.description: Starting a graphical app from foot, kitty or Alacritty hides the terminal until the app closes.

entries.label: Snap floating windows
entries.description: Floating windows stick to screen edges and to other windows while you drag them.

entries.label: Paste with middle click
entries.description: Middle-clicking pastes the text you last selected, without copying it first.

entries.label: Variable refresh rate (FreeSync/G-Sync)
entries.description: Lets the monitor follow the frame rate of games and videos to avoid stutter.

options.label: Always
options.description: Always on; some screens flicker in menus or on the desktop.

options.label: Fullscreen only
options.description: On while any window fills the screen.

options.label: Fullscreen games only
options.description: On only for fullscreen windows that report game or video content.

entries.help: “Fullscreen games only” is the safest choice: some screens flicker with it always on. A display's own setting on the Displays page wins over this one.

entries.label: Allow tearing in games
entries.description: Games marked for it show each frame as soon as it is ready: less delay, but a horizontal tear can appear.
entries.help: Only applies to windows with the immediate rule (Steam games, .exe titles and Minecraft in rules.lua).

entries.label: Back to the previous workspace
entries.description: Going to the workspace you are already on takes you back to the one you came from.
entries.help: For example, on workspace 3, press Super+3 to return to the workspace you were on before.

options.label: Across all monitors
options.description: Goes back to the last workspace you used on any monitor.

options.label: Per monitor
options.description: Each monitor remembers its own previous workspace.

entries.label: Open apps where you launched them
entries.description: A slow app opens on the workspace you started it from, even if you switched workspaces meanwhile.

options.label: Off
options.description: Windows open on the workspace you are on when they appear.

options.label: First window
options.description: Only the app's first window goes to the workspace it was started from.

options.label: Every window
options.description: Every window of the app, including later ones, goes there.

entries.label: Invert workspace swipe
entries.description: Swap which way a four-finger swipe moves between workspaces.

entries.label: Swipe distance
entries.description: How far your fingers travel for a full workspace change, in pixels.

entries.label: Swipe to a new workspace
entries.description: Swiping right past the last workspace creates a new one.

entries.label: Custom rules file
entries.description: Opens hypr/custom/rules.lua, where your own rules go; the built-in ones stay in the dotfiles.
